MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the total value of the digit 7 in 27,150? (1 mark)
   A. 700
   B. 7,000
   C. 70,000
   D. 7

2. Which of these is a factor of 40? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 7
   C. 10
   D. 6

3. Which of these shows 841 in words? (1 mark)
   A. eight hundred and forty-one
   B. eight hundred and fifty-one
   C. eight hundred and fourteen
   D. nine hundred and forty-one

4. Which is the largest number: 538, 583, 358, 385? (1 mark)
   A. 538
   B. 385
   C. 583
   D. 358

5. Which sentence about factors and multiples is correct? (1 mark)
   A. A number has more factors than multiples
   B. Factors of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on; multiples are 1, 2, 3 and 6
   C. Factors and multiples are the same thing
   D. Factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6; multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on

6. What is the rule of the pattern 750, 1,000, 1,250, 1,500? (1 mark)
   A. add 500
   B. add 750
   C. subtract 250
   D. add 250

7. Which number must be added to 3,425 to make 5,743? (1 mark)
   A. 2,318
   B. 2,418
   C. 9,168
   D. 2,308

8. Work out 8,421 − 6,537. (1 mark)
   A. 1,784
   B. 1,894
   C. 1,884
   D. 2,116

9. What is 48 × 20? (1 mark)
   A. 68
   B. 960
   C. 96
   D. 9,600

10. Estimate 24 × 18 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 400
   B. 500
   C. 300
   D. 4,000

11. What is 48 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 480
   B. 4,800
   C. 148
   D. 48,000

12. A remainder must always be (1 mark)
   A. bigger than the divisor
   B. equal to the divisor
   C. smaller than the divisor
   D. equal to the quotient

13. What is 79 ÷ 8? (1 mark)
   A. 9 remainder 8
   B. 8 remainder 15
   C. 9 remainder 7
   D. 10 remainder 7

14. What is 300 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 30
   B. 300
   C. 4
   D. 3

15. 45 eggs are packed in trays that each hold 6 eggs. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 6
   C. 7
   D. 8

16. What is 3/5 of 25? (1 mark)
   A. 20
   B. 5
   C. 15
   D. 10

17. What is 2/5 of 30? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 12
   C. 6
   D. 18

18. Dan writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 8/3
   B. 13/6
   C. 4 2/3
   D. 1/2

19. Simplify a + a + a. (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. a3
   C. 3a
   D. a + 3

20. If k = 3, what is the value of 5k − 2? (1 mark)
   A. 17
   B. 1
   C. 13
   D. 52

21. Simplify 8y + 2 − 3y. (1 mark)
   A. 11y + 2
   B. 5y − 2
   C. 5y + 2
   D. 7y

22. If x = 10, what is the value of x ÷ 2 + 1? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 1
   C. 6
   D. 5

23. What does 4m mean? (1 mark)
   A. 4 − m
   B. 4 × m
   C. 4 ÷ m
   D. 4 + m

24. Which unit is best for measuring the length of a classroom? (1 mark)
   A. Kilograms
   B. Centimetres only
   C. Metres
   D. Litres

25. What is half a metre in centimetres? (1 mark)
   A. 20 cm
   B. 5 cm
   C. 50 cm
   D. 500 cm

26. Change 1,200 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 1 m 20 cm
   B. 12 m 50 cm
   C. 12 m
   D. 13 m

27. Which shape has the same number of rows and columns of unit squares? (1 mark)
   A. A square
   B. A rectangle that is not a square
   C. A circle
   D. A triangle

28. A garden bed marked in 1 m squares has 9 rows and 4 columns. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 13 square metres
   B. 26 square metres
   C. 36 square metres
   D. 49 square metres

29. A cuboid is 7 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 42 blocks
   B. 21 blocks
   C. 12 blocks
   D. 49 blocks

30. What is 5 L − 2 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 1/2 L
   B. 3 L
   C. 2 1/4 L
   D. 2 3/4 L

31. How many days are in 6 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 144 days
   B. 30 days
   C. 42 days
   D. 49 days

32. School ends at a quarter past three in the afternoon. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 3:15 p.m.
   B. 15:3 p.m.
   C. 3:45 p.m.
   D. 3:15 a.m.

33. Change 35 days to weeks and days. (1 mark)
   A. 5 weeks 1 days
   B. 5 weeks
   C. 0 weeks 5 days
   D. 6 weeks

34. Kip faces North and makes a half turn. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. North
   C. West
   D. South

35. Kip faces North and makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. South
   C. West
   D. East

36. How many right angles are there in a rectangle? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 3
   C. 4
   D. 1

37. How many right angles make a straight line? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 3
   C. 4
   D. 1

38. A door has four straight sides and four square corners, with two long sides and two short sides. What shape is its face? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle
   B. Square
   C. Circle
   D. Triangle

39. In a tally chart, 3 groups of five and 1 more single tally mark are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 17
   B. 16
   C. 15
   D. 21

40. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. car
   B. walking
   C. bicycle
   D. bus

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Sort these fractions into proper, improper and mixed: 3/8, 11/5, 2 1/2, 9/9, 7/10. (4 marks)

42. Explain how multiplication can be used to check that 72 ÷ 6 = 12. (3 marks)

43. A trader has 12 kg of beans and 8 kg of maize. He sells 5 kg of the beans. Find the total mass of the beans and maize he has left. (3 marks)

44. A shop earned Ksh 4,750 on Monday and Ksh 3,895 on Tuesday. How much did it earn on the two days? (3 marks)

45. Explain why the parts must be equal when we write a fraction such as 1/4. (2 marks)

46. A sweet costs 50 cents. How many sweets can be bought with Ksh 10? (3 marks)

47. Draw a triangle and write down its number of sides and corners. (2 marks)

48. List all the factors of 36. (3 marks)

49. A triangle has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Find its perimeter. (2 marks)

50. 45 eggs are packed in trays that hold 6 eggs each. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? Explain. (3 marks)

51. The table shows football 5, netball 3, athletics 1 and swimming 1 for 10 pupils. Which sport is the most popular? How many pupils chose netball or athletics? (3 marks)

52. Add 1 1/4 L and 2 1/2 L. Show your working. (3 marks)

53. Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction and then change your answer back to an improper fraction to check it. (4 marks)

54. A rectangle has an area of 48 square units and 6 rows. How many columns does it have? Explain how you found out. (3 marks)

55. Estimate 5,382 + 3,617 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. Then find the exact sum. (4 marks)

56. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. Draw it roughly, label the sides and find its perimeter. (3 marks)

57. A tally chart shows walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1 and car 1 for 10 pupils. How many pupils walk to school? How many do not walk? (3 marks)

58. A learner says 3 weeks is 20 days. Explain her mistake and give the correct number of days. (3 marks)

59. Write 4, 6 and 9 as Roman numerals. (3 marks)

60. Ten vehicles passed: 5 matatus, 2 boda bodas, 2 buses and 1 lorry. Draw a table to show this data. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — 7,000
   The digit 7 is in the thousands place, so its total value is 7 × 1,000 = 7,000.

2. C — 10
   40 ÷ 10 = 4 with nothing left over, so 10 is a factor of 40. The others leave a remainder.

3. A — eight hundred and forty-one
   841 = eight hundred and forty-one. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

4. C — 583
   Compare the digits from the left. The largest number is 583.

5. D — Factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6; multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on
   Factors divide a number exactly and are few. Multiples are found by multiplying and go on and on.

6. D — add 250
   Each number is 250 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 250.

7. A — 2,318
   5,743 − 3,425 = 2,318. Check: 3,425 + 2,318 = 5,743.

8. C — 1,884
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 8,421 − 6,537 = 1,884. Check: 1,884 + 6,537 = 8,421.

9. B — 960
   48 × 2 = 96, then × 10 gives 960.

10. A — 400
   24 rounds to 20 and 18 rounds to 20. 20 × 20 = 400.

11. B — 4,800
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 48 × 100 = 4,800.

12. C — smaller than the divisor
   If the remainder were as big as the divisor, another whole group could still be made.

13. C — 9 remainder 7
   8 × 9 = 72 and 79 − 72 = 7. So 79 ÷ 8 = 9 remainder 7. Check: 9 × 8 + 7 = 79.

14. D — 3
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 300 ÷ 100 = 3.

15. D — 8
   45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3. The 3 left-over eggs need one more tray, so 8 trays are needed.

16. C — 15
   25 ÷ 5 = 5 and 5 × 3 = 15. So 3/5 of 25 is 15.

17. B — 12
   30 ÷ 5 = 6 and 6 × 2 = 12. So 2/5 of 30 is 12.

18. D — 1/2
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 1/2 is less than one whole.

19. C — 3a
   Only like terms can be joined. a + a + a = 3a.

20. C — 13
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 13.

21. C — 5y + 2
   Only like terms can be joined. 8y + 2 − 3y = 5y + 2.

22. C — 6
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 6.

23. B — 4 × m
   A number written next to a letter means multiply. 4m is 4 times m.

24. C — Metres
   A classroom is several metres long, so metres are the sensible unit.

25. C — 50 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: half a metre in centimetres is 50 cm.

26. C — 12 m
   1,200 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 0. So 1,200 cm = 12 m.

27. A — A square
   A square has equal sides, so its number of rows equals its number of columns.

28. C — 36 square metres
   9 × 4 = 36 square metres.

29. A — 42 blocks
   One layer has 7 × 3 = 21 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 21 × 2 = 42 blocks.

30. A — 2 1/2 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 5 L − 2 1/2 L = 2 1/2 L.

31. C — 42 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 6 × 7 = 42 days.

32. A — 3:15 p.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 3:15 p.m..

33. B — 5 weeks
   35 ÷ 7 = 5 remainder 0, so 35 days = 5 weeks.

34. D — South
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a half turn gives South.

35. C — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a three-quarter turn clockwise gives West.

36. C — 4
   A rectangle has four corners and each is a right angle.

37. A — 2
   A straight line is a half turn, which is two right angles.

38. A — Rectangle
   Opposite sides are equal but not all sides are equal, so it is a rectangle.

39. B — 16
   3 × 5 + 1 = 16.

40. B — walking
   The biggest number is 6, which belongs to walking.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Proper: 3/8 and 7/10. Improper: 11/5 and 9/9. Mixed: 2 1/2.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group and 1 mark for placing all five correctly.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Multiply the answer by the divisor: 12 × 6 = 72. This gives the starting number, so the division is correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for multiplying the answer by the divisor, 1 mark for 12 × 6 = 72, 1 mark for the conclusion.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 15 kg
   Working / marking points: 12 − 5 = 7 kg of beans (1 mark); 7 + 8 (1 mark); 15 kg (1 mark).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 8,645
   Working / marking points: 4,750 + 3,895. Ones 5; tens 5 + 9 = 14 write 4 carry 1; hundreds 7 + 8 + 1 = 16 write 6 carry 1; thousands 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. 1 mark for setting up, 1 for regrouping, 1 for the answer with units.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. If the parts are different in size, one part is not one quarter of the whole.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying parts must be equal in size and 1 mark for the reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20 sweets
   Working / marking points: Ksh 10 = 1,000 cents (1 mark); 1,000 ÷ 50 (1 mark); 20 sweets (1 mark).

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: A drawing of a triangle with 3 straight sides. It has 3 sides and 3 corners.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drawing and 1 mark for the numbers.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36
   Working / marking points: Pairs: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. 3 marks for all nine factors, 2 marks for seven or eight, 1 mark for at least five.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: 12 cm
   Working / marking points: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12. 1 mark for adding all three sides and 1 mark for the unit.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: 8 trays
   Working / marking points: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3 (1 mark). Seven trays are full (1 mark). The 3 left-over eggs need another tray, so 8 trays (1 mark).

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Football is the most popular. 3 + 1 = 4 pupils chose netball or athletics.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for football, 1 mark for 3 + 1, 1 mark for 4.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Wholes 1 + 2 = 3 (1 mark); parts 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4 (1 mark); total 3 3/4 L (1 mark).

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: 11/4 = 2 3/4. Check: 2 × 4 = 8 and 8 + 3 = 11, so 11/4.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 2 3/4 with working, 2 marks for the correct check.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: 8 columns. Area = rows × columns, so columns = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the relationship, 1 mark for the division, 1 mark for 8.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 5,380 + 3,620 = 9,000. Exact: 8,999.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for the estimate 9,000, 1 mark for the exact sum 8,999.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Perimeter = 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a labelled rectangle, 1 mark for adding all four sides, 1 mark for 26 cm.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6 pupils walk. 10 − 6 = 4 pupils do not walk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 6, 1 mark for 10 − 6, 1 mark for 4.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 week has 7 days, so 3 weeks is 3 × 7 = 21 days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7 days in a week, 1 mark for multiplying by 3, 1 mark for 21 days.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: IV, VI, IX
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each. IV is 5 − 1, VI is 5 + 1, IX is 10 − 1.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: A table with a title and two columns, Vehicle and Number, with rows matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1 and total 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for title and headings, 1 mark for all four rows correct, 1 mark for the total 10.
